bridge: Builds on M05 evidence/uncertainty, A02 definitions and the technical topic of your selected paper.
teaching:
A paper's claim is narrower than its title. Identify the question, threat model, assumptions, method, baseline and evidence. Separate what the authors demonstrate from what they propose or speculate. A strong result can still depend on a restricted platform or dataset.

Read in passes. First map the claim and figures; next inspect definitions and method; finally follow the proof or experiment details. Keep a glossary of unfamiliar notation and return to prerequisite material before treating it as understood. A summary that only repeats the abstract does not evaluate evidence.

For empirical work, inspect dataset provenance, splits, units of analysis, confounders and artifact availability. For proofs, inspect the game, allowed adversary and assumptions. Cite exact sections supporting each conclusion and state missing evidence. The fictional abstract below provides a complete first exercise without requiring subscription access.
example:
Fictional abstract
Rule R detects9 of10 labelled incidents on one training host and alerts on5 of90 benign events.
Authors claim it improves safety across all enterprise systems.
Method: choose rule thresholds using all100 events.
No independent test set; no artifact/version record.
Evidence supports performance on the supplied training sample, not universal deployment.
explanation: Precision is 9/14≈64.3% and recall90%. Choosing thresholds on the same dataset used to report performance creates an optimism risk. The broad enterprise claim exceeds one-host evidence. This critique does not prove the rule is useless; it specifies what additional evidence is needed.
exercise: Write a structured review of the fictional abstract with claim, supported result, two limitations, missing artifacts and a proposed independent validation. Calculate precision/recall.
solution: Identify training/test reuse and limited host sampling. Request versioned rules/data provenance and an untouched representative test set. Avoid substituting accuracy for operational false-alert burden.
challenge: Select one open paper from an assigned advanced reading. Produce a one-page claim/evidence table with section references and three prerequisite concepts. Distinguish a paper limitation from an error you have actually demonstrated.
challenge_solution: The submission should let a reviewer locate evidence and see uncertainty. Unperformed reproduction is a limitation, not proof of an incorrect result. A specific defect requires a supported counterexample or inconsistency.
